23228639.fullDescription:
InternScience Agents-A1 MoE agentic vision-language model served via llama.cpp — optimized for Olares One.
Multimodal: accepts images via OpenAI-compatible vision API (image_url format).
RTX 5090M (24GB) + 96GB DDR5 + Core Ultra 9 275HX.

48930371.name: dockerbuilderone
48930371.description: Build Docker images from uploaded Dockerfile folders and push to ghcr.io
48930371.title: Docker Builder One
48930371.fullDescription:
Web UI for building container images on Olares One without leaving the browser.

Upload a zip of your Dockerfile project (persists under appData/dockerbuilder/projects).
Builder runtime: pytorch/pytorch:2.12.0-cuda13.0-cudnn9-devel.
Builds use Kaniko from docker.io/martizih/kaniko (no privileged DinD — Olares OPA safe).
Kaniko executor is copied from the init container into /tools/kaniko/executor at pod start.
Kaniko layer cache is local only at appData/dockerbuilder/kaniko-cache (--no-push-cache);
set KANIKO_CACHE_REPO for remote cache. If base image pulls fail, set KANIKO_REGISTRY_MIRROR
or retry the build.

Builds run one at a time via an async queue worker; additional start_build requests are
queued with position shown in the UI and MCP get_build_queue. Queue order persists in
appData/dockerbuilder/jobs/queue.json across restarts.

Kaniko build+push streams live logs in the UI to ghcr.io using your GitHub PAT
(OLARES_USER_GITHUB_TOKEN).

Image must be ghcr.io/<user>/<repo>:<tag> — e.g. ghcr.io/<your-github-user>/my-app:1.0.0.
Uses OLARES_USER_GITHUB_USERNAME from your Olares user environment for ghcr.io login.

After push, make the package public at github.com/users/<user>/packages or configure
imagePullSecrets on apps that consume the image.

MCP (streamable HTTP) for agents: connect to /mcp/mcp on port 8080 (authLevel internal).
In-cluster: http://dockerbuilderone:8080/mcp/mcp or entrance dockerbuildermcp.
Tools: health_check, list_projects, upload_project (base64 zip), list_builds,
get_build_queue, get_build, get_build_logs, start_build, cancel_build.
Discovery: GET /api/mcp or /health. Optional MCP_CORS_ORIGIN=* (default).
MCP Host checks off by default (Olares entrance Host). Harden: MCP_DNS_REBINDING_PROTECTION=1
and MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=your-host.example.com:*,dockerbuilderone:*.

v1.0.13: LLM_REASONING on|off|auto env — no more hardcoded --reasoning off.
v1.0.12: reuse GGUFs already in Common/comfyui/model/llms (and subdirs) via symlink — official ComfyUI migrates External/ai/model/llms there; skip redownload.
v1.0.10: llama.cpp defaults — drop --mlock; ensure GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT=1 + --op-offload.
v1.0.9: trim CPU/memory requests for denser multi-app packing (llm).

v1.0.5: migrate to apiVersion v3 shared chart (Olares 1.12.6+). Flatten server+client; workloadReplicas; no OLARES_USER_* in templates.
v1.0.3: fix potential ????/ //// garbage — drop lordx64 external jinja (redacted_im_end
breaks peg-native); use GGUF embedded template + --reasoning off (same fix as Qwythos v1.0.6).
v1.0.2: attempted lordx64 jinja override (same class of bug).
v2.0.8: **fix CrashLoopBackOff on fresh install** (Discord-reported by user eahnlk, 2026-06-09). The chart writes its ~18 GB model cache to `/olares/share/ai/model/llms/` via hostPath. On a fresh Olares install where no other app has written to this path before, the dir is owned uid 1000 mode 755. The buun-llama-cpp image runs as a non-root `appuser` (UID ≠ 1000): can read (755 lets "others" read) but cannot write → curl write fails → container exits within seconds → CrashLoopBackOff. Fix: add a trusted root chmod init (`beclab/aboveos-busybox:1.37.0`; historically alpine) that `chmod -R 777 /olares/share/ai/model` before the main container starts. Same llama-server config otherwise (buun:87c351d2, asym q8_0-K/turbo4-V KV, MTP n=3, mmproj-gpu-swap, 262K context, --reasoning off).

v2.0.7: **rollback BeeLlama → buun (Hermes tool-calling regression fix)**. v2.0.6 swapped image to `ghcr.io/anbeeld/beellama.cpp:server-cuda13-v0.3.1` for slightly higher MTP accept rate, but a user reported on Discord that their Hermes Agent flow stopped working after the upgrade. BeeLlama v0.3.1 has a chat-parser/tool-call detection behavior difference vs spiritbuun `buun-llama-cpp:87c351d2`. Reverting the image to the known-good `aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:87c351d2` while keeping everything else identical (asym q8_0-K/turbo4-V KV, MTP n=3, mmproj-gpu-swap, 262K context, `--reasoning off`). Bench unchanged from v2.0.5 (~240 t/s, 84-88% accept). Will re-evaluate BeeLlama once the parser regression is fixed upstream.

v2.0.6: ~~upgrade to BeeLlama v0.3.1~~ (rolled back in v2.0.7 due to Hermes tool-calling regression).

v2.0.5: **asymmetric KV cache** (free K quality boost). Image bump 316e88e → 87c351d2 (spiritbuun fused asymmetric flash-attn kernel, 2026-06-04). KV config: symmetric q4_0/q4_0 → asymmetric q8_0-K + turbo4-V. Keys at 8-bit (high attention quality), values at turbo4 (compressed). Native 262K context preserved (smaller Q3_K_XL model has the headroom that abliterated Q4_K does not). Also dropped deprecated `--chat-template-kwargs` for `--reasoning off` flag. Bench Olares One (3 runs Space Invaders): 236.28 / 243.32 / 241.87 t/s = AVG 240.5 t/s with 84-88% MTP accept (vs v1.0.1 baseline 243.59 t/s, -1% speed for measurable K precision uplift). Quality > 1% raw speed for long-context use.

v2.0.0: **vision UNLOCKED on the champion via spiritbuun `--mmproj-gpu-swap`**. The vision regression from v1.0.4/v1.0.5 that forced us back to text-only in v1.0.6 is now solved by a much cleverer mechanism than "shrink context to make room for mmproj". The new buun-llama-cpp image (`aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:316e88e`) ships spiritbuun's `--mmproj-gpu-swap` feature: keeps mmproj on CPU at startup, swaps MTP out of VRAM when an image arrives, loads mmproj to GPU for fast encoding (~1-2s), then swaps back. MTP has no persistent state so the swap is lossless.

**Bench validated 2026-05-24 on Olares One**:
- Text decode: **243.59 t/s AVG** (10 runs, range 237.60-251.39) — only -2.8% vs v1.0.6 text-only baseline (250.54)
- Vision test: 64×64 PNG → "Red" correct, **1.13s total** for swap + encode + generate
- Swap latencies: MTP→mmproj 213ms, mmproj→MTP 540ms (~750ms vision overhead per request)
- Auto-fit context: **262K full native** (vs 64K in v1.0.4/v1.0.5 attempts) — `--mmproj-gpu-swap` frees enough VRAM that the full window fits

**Single endpoint now handles everything**:
- Text generation at near-champion speed (243 t/s)
- Vision input via OpenAI-compatible `image_url`
- Tool calling (Hermes Agent compatible) via `--jinja`
- Full 262K context window
- MTP at 86.6% draft acceptance

Stack:
- Image: `aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:316e88e` — spiritbuun fork at upstream-merge commit (post llama.cpp master + mmproj-gpu-swap + GDN tensor-split fixes)
- Target model: `lordx64/Qwable-v1-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL (17.2 GB)
- Vision encoder: `mmproj-BF16.gguf` from same repo (~900 MB, CPU-resident at idle, GPU-resident during image requests)
- `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --mmproj-gpu-swap`
- q4_0 KV cache, flash attention, auto-fit context

**Why we're confident in this build**: we built it yesterday (`aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:316e88e`, downstream of spiritbuun commit `316e88e` which adds `--mmproj-gpu-swap` docs after the feature merge at `8e64d7a`). Validated end-to-end today: text decode tight (σ ≈ 4), vision correct on color test, no cycle bug.

Trade-off vs v1.0.6 text-only: -2.8% throughput + ~750ms per vision request. In exchange: vision + 4× more context. Worth it for any agentic workflow that mixes text and screenshots.

v1.0.6: **revert to text-only champion config**. v1.0.4/v1.0.5 attempted to add mmproj vision encoder but the MTP + mmproj + 192K/64K ctx combo blew the 24 GB VRAM budget (compute pp buffer alone needed ~4 GB at ubatch 2048). Trade-off was not worth it — text speed dropped, context shrank, and stability was fragile. Back to v1.0.3 config: **262K full native context, 246 t/s MTP champion, no vision**. For vision use cases, use `llamacppqwen36beellamavision1` (Qwen 3.6 27B dense + BeeLlama + mmproj, 106 t/s @ 200K vision) or `vllmgemma426ba4bvisionone` (Gemma 4 + native multimodal, 135 t/s but lower tool-calling reliability).

v1.0.4: **vision unlocked** (rolled back in v1.0.6). Add `--mmproj /models/mmproj-BF16.gguf` (~900 MB, downloaded automatically from `lordx64/Qwable-v1-GGUF`). Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B is natively multimodal (vision encoder shipped by Alibaba) and llama.cpp mainline supports `--spec-type draft-mtp` + `--mmproj` together since the MTP merge (b9274+).

**Why this matters for agentic use**: Hermes-Agent style tool calling can now consume images directly through the same endpoint that already wins on BFCL/SWE-bench. No more split between a Qwen text agent and a Gemma vision sibling — one model, one GPU slot, full vision + text + tool calling.

Args changes vs v1.0.3:
- `--mmproj $MODELS_DIR/mmproj-BF16.gguf` added
- `--ubatch-size 512 → 2048` (mandatory: ubatch must be ≥ image_max_tokens or vision encoder asserts per PR #21550)
- `--batch-size 512 → 2048` (matches ubatch)
- `CTX_SIZE 262144 → 196608` (192K — gives ~1 GB headroom for mmproj VRAM on 24 GB GPU)

VRAM budget @ 64K (corrected in v1.0.5, then reverted in v1.0.6):
- Model Q3_K_XL: 17.2 GB
- mmproj BF16: 1.0 GB
- KV q4_0 @ 64K: 0.8 GB
- MTP draft buffer @ n_max=1: ~1.3 GB
- Compute pp buffer @ ubatch 2048: ~2.0 GB
- **Total: ~22.3 GB / 23.4 GB usable** (fit but very tight, abandoned in v1.0.6)

Image input via OpenAI-compatible `image_url` (base64 data URI or URL). Expected perf: ~240-245 t/s text decode (down from 249, the 2048 ubatch costs ~2% on pure text but is required once mmproj is loaded). Vision prompt processing on mmproj BF16: tested on Olares One in prior Qwen vision work, comfortable headroom.

v1.0.3: bump image `aamsellem/llama-cpp-mtp:master-ad27757` → `master-bb28c1f`. Picks up am17an's PR [#23461](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/23461) "server: free draft/MTP resources on sleep to fix VRAM leak" (community Reddit thread confirms necessity on b9274) + #23433 "mtp: use inp_out_ids for skipping logit computation" + #23131 SWA null-buffer fix. Bench re-validated 2026-05-22: 250.08 t/s AVG (10 runs, +0.3% vs ad27757 — noise). Real value is sustained-load stability (VRAM leak fix matters for agentic sessions hours-long).

v1.0.2: bump default `CTX_SIZE` from 32K to **262144 (full native Qwen3.6 35B-A3B context window)**. Context sweep validated 2026-05-21 on Olares One showing essentially zero throughput regression across context sizes:

| Context | t/s AVG | runs | delta vs 32K |
|---------|--------:|-----:|-------------:|
| 32K | 249.30 | 10 | baseline |
| 64K | 252.64 | 5 | +1.3% (noise) |
| 128K | 250.39 | 5 | +0.4% (noise) |
| **262K (full native)** | **245.71** | 5 | -1.4% |

Memory budget at 262K Q3_K_XL + q4_0 KV + MTP draft buffer:
- Model: 17.2 GB
- q4_0 KV @ 262K (32 layers × 262K × 2 KV): ~3.2 GB
- MTP draft compute buffer: ~1 GB
- Compute buffer: ~0.5 GB
- Total: ~21.9 GB / 23.42 GB usable on 24 GB GPU (HAMi overhead-accounted)

Comfortable headroom. Full 262K context is essentially free on this stack — the MoE-A3B + MTP path doesn't have the per-token cost scaling with context that dense models exhibit (Mamba-like state-space layers carry constant per-token cost regardless of position).

Practically: this app is now **fastest AND longest-context** Qwen3.6 27B/35B path on Olares One. Beats `llamacppqwen36beellamaone` v1.0.4 (107 t/s @ 262K, dense + DFlash) by **+130%** at the same context window. Beats `llamacppqwen36mtpone` v1.0.9 (74 t/s @ 262K, dense + MTP) by **+232%**. Same image as both (`aamsellem/llama-cpp-mtp:master-ad27757`), different model + architecture pays off entirely.

v1.0.1: complete rebuild. Switch to MTP path with `aamsellem/llama-cpp-mtp:master-ad27757` (ggml-org/llama.cpp master HEAD with PR #22673 MTP + #23269 cleanup + #23287 NVIDIA backend sampling + #22522 PDL Hopper+). Swap target from `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF` Q4_K_XL → `lordx64/Qwable-v1-GGUF` Q3_K_XL (Q4_K_XL=22 GB OOMs with KV at 24 GB; Q3_K_XL=17.2 GB fits comfortably). Args: `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --ctx-size 32768 --cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0 --batch-size 512 --ubatch-size 512 --parallel 1 --flash-attn on --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'`.

**Bench validated 2026-05-21 on Olares One**: **249.30 t/s AVG** (10 runs, range 10.15, σ ≈ 3.0), **86.6% draft acceptance** (range 83.8–89.0%). NEW absolute champion on Olares One:
- +37% vs Nemotron-Labs 30B-A3B NVFP4 + vLLM #40082 (182.14 t/s)
- +83% vs Gemma 4 26B-A4B vLLM (135.97 t/s)
- +132% vs BeeLlama Qwen3.6 27B + DFlash (107.54 t/s)
- +236% vs Qwen3.6 27B dense MTP same image (74.28 t/s)

Why so fast: MoE-A3B = only ~3B params active per token (per-token compute is roughly that of a 3B model) + MTP at 86.6% accept (drafts almost always validate) + NVIDIA backend sampling moves draft sampling onto CUDA backend (fewer host roundtrips). Effective: "3B-active speed with 35B-breadth quality." Context limited to 32K because KV cache + MTP draft buffer fits on 24 GB; higher contexts would need IQ4_XS or larger memory.

Title renamed "Qwen 36B-A3B One" → "Qwen36 35B-A3B MTP" for clarity. Port 8080 → 8000 (matches llama-server default in our master image).

v1.0.0: initial release. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Apache 2.0, April 2026). Same hybrid SSM/MoE architecture as 3.5 — reuses proven Olares One config (llama.cpp b8740, UD-Q4_K_XL, KV q4_0 with Hadamard rotation, batch 2048/ubatch 1024, 64K ctx). SWE-bench 70.0→73.4, Terminal-Bench 40.5→51.5.

18c47618.name: browserlessone
18c47618.description: Browserless headless Chromium for Puppeteer and Playwright on Olares One
18c47618.title: Browserless One
18c47618.fullDescription:
Self-hosted Browserless Chromium (ghcr.io/browserless/chromium) on port 3000.
Connect Puppeteer or Playwright to ws://browserlessone:3000. REST API docs at /docs.
App entrance opens the live debugger at /debugger/?token=YOUR_TOKEN (Browserless v2 requires token + trailing slash).
Set BROWSERLESS_PROXY_URL to your public app URL (e.g. https://APPID.user.olares.com) so debugger session links work.
Playwright chromium.connect() runs automation but sessions may not appear in debugger; use Puppeteer/CDP for live debugger view.
Default token is browserlessone — change BROWSERLESS_TOKEN in Settings → Application before exposing publicly.
KEEP_ALIVE=true is set per upstream env name; note Browserless v2 OSS may log this
variable as deprecated — use launch URL ttl/keepalive query params for session timing.
CONCURRENT=5, QUEUED=10, TIMEOUT=300000 ms, HEALTH=true, 2 GiB /dev/shm for stable Chrome.
Data and downloads persist under appData/browserless. Non-commercial SSPL; commercial use needs a license.

  COLIBRI_RAM_GB: planner budget GiB (default 48; not an OS hard limit)
  LLM_API_KEY: optional API key for OpenAI gateway
  HF_TOKEN: required for large gated/rate-limited download

Disk: need ~180 GB free under /olares/share/ai/model (shared).
First boot: clone + compile + ~155 GB download — hours.

License: DeepSeek model license. Engine: see JustVugg/colibri.

In-cluster: http://cosyvoice3one:8000
Shared entrance: http://<route-id>.shared.olares.com
App entrance (proxy): port 8080

--- OpenAI-compatible speech ---

curl -X POST http://cosyvoice3one:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"你好，欢迎使用 CosyVoice3。","voice":"<registered-voice>","response_format":"wav"}' \
  -o out.wav

curl -X POST http://cosyvoice3one:8000/v1/audio/speech/clone \
  -F "text=你好啊，食咗饭未啊？" \
  -F "voice=@./cantonese_ref.wav" \
  -o yue.wav

--- Cantonese ---

Pass Cantonese text with a Cantonese reference voice for best results.
Instruct/dialect modes follow CosyVoice3 docs (18 Chinese dialects).

First boot downloads ~10GB model to shared HF cache
/olares/share/ai/model/speech/huggingface (reused by other speech apps).
Image: ghcr.io/hsiang-han/cosyvoice3-api (CUDA 12.8, Blackwell OK).

26f6a12d.name: llamacppdsv4flash0731one
26f6a12d.title: DSV4 Flash cpu-moe
26f6a12d.fullDescription:
EXPERIMENTAL — DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (284B total / ~21B activated MoE) via GGUF
hybrid offload on Olares One (96GB DDR5 + RTX 5090M 24GB).

  Weights (default): Unsloth UD-IQ2_XXS 3-shard (~90.9 GB) — fits 96GB with tight headroom
  Optional: UD-IQ3_XXS 4-shard (~104 GB) — may thrash; set DSV4_QUANT=iq3_xxs only if you accept swap
  Runtime: nvidia/cuda:13.1.0-devel builds ggml-org/llama.cpp (DeepSeek V4 + draft-dspark)
  Hybrid: --cpu-moe (routed experts in RAM via mmap) + -ngl 99 (attn/shared on GPU)
  Spec: ENABLE_DSPARK=0 (default) — Q8_0 DSpark ~10.9 GB often blows RAM with IQ2
    Set ENABLE_DSPARK=1 only with free RAM; watch draft acceptance in logs
  Defaults (DeepSeek recommended): temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 0, ctx 131072
    Override ctx via LLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW if KV thrash
  Batch 2048 / ubatch 1024; --threads 22; CPU limit 22

Editable knobs (Settings → Application):
  LLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW: default 131072 if unset
  DSV4_QUANT: iq2_xxs (default) | iq3_xxs
  ENABLE_CPU_MOE: 1 (default)
  N_CPU_MOE: optional partial --n-cpu-moe N
  ENABLE_NO_MMAP: 1 only if forced RAM load needed
  N_GPU_LAYERS: override -ngl (default 99)
  ENABLE_DSPARK: 0 (default) — downloads dspark-*-Q8_0.gguf when 1
  OVERRIDE_TENSORS: extra -ot patterns
  HF_TOKEN / HF_ENDPOINT: user Integration mirror (e.g. https://hf-mirror.com) + token

Expectation: hybrid MoE disk/RAM-bound TG — not a full-GPU speed chart.
HF token + mirror recommended for ~91 GB download (stalls common on huggingface.co).

License: DeepSeek model license. Engine: MIT (llama.cpp).

e8cc7f19.fullDescription:
EXPERIMENTAL — Laguna S 2.1 (117.6B total / 8.5B activated MoE) on Olares One via GGUF
hybrid offload. Official NVFP4 (~71 GB) targets ~128 GB unified (Spark / Mac Studio).

    experts Q4_K (imatrix), signal path Q8_0 — from poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-GGUF
    Abiray IQ4_XS broken (split.count=2, single file) — do not use
  Runtime: nvidia/cuda:13.1.0-devel builds poolsideai/llama.cpp @ 04b2b72 (branch laguna)
  Hybrid: --cpu-moe (all routed experts in RAM via mmap) + -ngl 99 (attn/shared on GPU)
  Spec: ENABLE_DFLASH=0 (default) — on cpu-moe, DFlash often low accept (~9%) and slows TG.
    Set ENABLE_DFLASH=1 only if slot logs show draft acceptance >>50%.
  Default ctx 16384 (raise via LLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW; native GGUF meta is 262144)
  Sampling (Poolside): temp 0.7 top_p 0.95
  Batch 2048 / ubatch 1024 (PP); mmap kept; --threads 22; CPU limit 22

Editable experiment knobs (Settings → Application):
  LAGUNA_QUANT: q4_k_m (default official) | iq4_xs | q2_k_xl | iq2_m | iq3_xxs
  ENABLE_CPU_MOE: 1 (default) — full --cpu-moe when N_CPU_MOE empty
  N_CPU_MOE: optional — if set, --n-cpu-moe N (some experts on GPU); leave empty for full CPU experts
  ENABLE_NO_MMAP: 1 only if you want forced RAM load (higher RSS; try if TG still page-faults)
  N_GPU_LAYERS: override -ngl (default 99)
  OVERRIDE_TENSORS: extra -ot patterns (comma-separated name=buft)
  ENABLE_DFLASH: 0 (default) — optional; check draft acceptance in logs

dcde86e3.name: llamacppnemotrondiffusion14b1
dcde86e3.description: NVIDIA Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion 14B — tri-mode (AR + parallel diffusion + self-spec) — first public diffusion LLM on consumer Blackwell
dcde86e3.title: Nemotron Diffusion 14B One
dcde86e3.fullDescription:
Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion 14B is a tri-mode language model from NVIDIA Nemotron Labs.
Same weights, three decoding strategies:
  1. AR (autoregressive) — standard token-by-token
  2. Diffusion — parallel multi-token generation via diffusion process
  3. Linear self-speculation — diffusion drafts + AR verifies (shared KV cache, no separate drafter file)

The spiritbuun/buun-llama-cpp fork (forked from TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant) added the diffusion patches.
NVIDIA's own Python reference OOMs on 14B at 24 GB VRAM — spiritbuun's GGUF Q8_0 quant + llama.cpp inference
is the first known path to run this model on a single consumer-grade Blackwell 24 GB GPU.

The self-speculation mode is enabled by default in llama-server; no extra --spec-type flag needed.
NVIDIA paper benchmarks: 5.9× tokens per forward over Qwen3-8B, 3× higher acceptance length than
Qwen3-8B-Eagle3, 2.2× speedup over Eagle3 in SGLang.

When to use:
  - You want to be on the bleeding edge of diffusion LLMs
  - You're benchmarking new spec-decoding paradigms on Olares
  - Tool calling and agent workflows where parallel-token speedup compounds

Custom image: docker.io/aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:316e88e
Fork source: https://github.com/spiritbuun/buun-llama-cpp
Model card: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-14B
GGUF: https://huggingface.co/spiritbuun/Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-14B-Q8_0-GGUF
dcde86e3.upgradeDescription:

v1.0.20: migrate to apiVersion v3 shared chart (Olares 1.12.6+). Flatten server+client; workloadReplicas; no OLARES_USER_* in templates.
v1.0.0: initial release. NVIDIA Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion 14B served via spiritbuun/buun-llama-cpp (custom fork with diffusion-mode patches). First public diffusion LLM runnable on consumer Blackwell mobile (RTX 5090M 24 GB) — NVIDIA's own Python reference OOMs on 14B at 24 GB. Stack: spiritbuun/Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-14B-Q8_0-GGUF (14.4 GB) + buun-llama-cpp:316e88e (2026-05-24) + auto-detected self-speculation. Tri-mode: AR / Diffusion parallel decoding / Linear self-speculation (k=4, recommended).

Reference benchmarks (RTX 3090 24 GB, spiritbuun): 42-50 t/s prose/code @ temp 0/0.7, 126-132 t/s short responses. Olares One (RTX 5090M sm_120) bench TBD on first install.

NVIDIA paper claims 2.7× speedup vs AR on DGX Spark 8B, 3.3× on GB200 8B. The diffusion mode's parallel-token generation unlocks throughput beyond what MTP/Eagle can achieve.

  - Image: docker.io/aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:316e88e

On a fresh Olares install where no other app has written to this path before, the dir is owned uid 1000 mode 755. The buun-llama-cpp image runs as a non-root `appuser` (UID ≠ 1000): can read (755 lets "others" read) but cannot write → curl write fails → container exits within seconds → CrashLoopBackOff. Fix: add a trusted root chmod init (`beclab/aboveos-busybox:1.37.0`; historically alpine) that `chmod -R 777 /olares/share/ai/model` before the main container starts. v2.0.0: **vision UNLOCKED on the champion via spiritbuun `--mmproj-gpu-swap`**. The vision regression from v1.0.4/v1.0.5 that forced us back to text-only in v1.0.6 is now solved by a much cleverer mechanism than "shrink context to make room for mmproj". The new buun-llama-cpp image (`aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:316e88e`) ships spiritbuun's `--mmproj-gpu-swap` feature: keeps mmproj on CPU at startup, swaps MTP out of VRAM when an image arrives, loads mmproj to GPU for fast encoding (~1-2s), then swaps back. MTP has no persistent state so the swap is lossless.

**Bench validated 2026-05-24 on Olares One**:
- Text decode: **243.59 t/s AVG** (10 runs, range 237.60-251.39) — only -2.8% vs v1.0.6 text-only baseline (250.54)
- Vision test: 64×64 PNG → "Red" correct, **1.13s total** for swap + encode + generate
- Swap latencies: MTP→mmproj 213ms, mmproj→MTP 540ms (~750ms vision overhead per request)
- Auto-fit context: **262K full native** (vs 64K in v1.0.4/v1.0.5 attempts) — `--mmproj-gpu-swap` frees enough VRAM that the full window fits

**Single endpoint now handles everything**:
- Text generation at near-champion speed (243 t/s)
- Vision input via OpenAI-compatible `image_url`
- Tool calling (Hermes Agent compatible) via `--jinja`
- Full 262K context window
- MTP at 86.6% draft acceptance

Stack:
- Image: `aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:316e88e` — spiritbuun fork at upstream-merge commit (post llama.cpp master + mmproj-gpu-swap + GDN tensor-split fixes)
- Target model: `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL (17.2 GB)
- Vision encoder: `mmproj-BF16.gguf` from same repo (~900 MB, CPU-resident at idle, GPU-resident during image requests)
- `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --mmproj-gpu-swap`
- q4_0 KV cache, flash attention, auto-fit context

**Why we're confident in this build**: we built it yesterday (`aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:316e88e`, downstream of spiritbuun commit `316e88e` which adds `--mmproj-gpu-swap` docs after the feature merge at `8e64d7a`). Validated end-to-end today: text decode tight (σ ≈ 4), vision correct on color test, no cycle bug.

Trade-off vs v1.0.6 text-only: -2.8% throughput + ~750ms per vision request. In exchange: vision + 4× more context. Worth it for any agentic workflow that mixes text and screenshots.

v1.0.6: **revert to text-only champion config**. v1.0.4/v1.0.5 attempted to add mmproj vision encoder but the MTP + mmproj + 192K/64K ctx combo blew the 24 GB VRAM budget (compute pp buffer alone needed ~4 GB at ubatch 2048). Trade-off was not worth it — text speed dropped, context shrank, and stability was fragile. Back to v1.0.3 config: **262K full native context, 246 t/s MTP champion, no vision**. For vision use cases, use `llamacppqwen36beellamavision1` (Qwen 3.6 27B dense + BeeLlama + mmproj, 106 t/s @ 200K vision) or `vllmgemma426ba4bvisionone` (Gemma 4 + native multimodal, 135 t/s but lower tool-calling reliability).

Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B is natively multimodal (vision encoder shipped by Alibaba) and llama.cpp mainline supports `--spec-type draft-mtp` + `--mmproj` together since the MTP merge (b9274+).

**Why this matters for agentic use**: Hermes-Agent style tool calling can now consume images directly through the same endpoint that already wins on BFCL/SWE-bench. No more split between a Qwen text agent and a Gemma vision sibling — one model, one GPU slot, full vision + text + tool calling.

v1.0.2: bump default `CTX_SIZE` from 32K to **262144 (full native Qwen3.6 35B-A3B context window)**. Context sweep validated 2026-05-21 on Olares One showing essentially zero throughput regression across context sizes:

| Context | t/s AVG | runs | delta vs 32K |
|---------|--------:|-----:|-------------:|
| 32K | 249.30 | 10 | baseline |
| 64K | 252.64 | 5 | +1.3% (noise) |
| 128K | 250.39 | 5 | +0.4% (noise) |
| **262K (full native)** | **245.71** | 5 | -1.4% |

Memory budget at 262K Q3_K_XL + q4_0 KV + MTP draft buffer:
- Model: 17.2 GB
- q4_0 KV @ 262K (32 layers × 262K × 2 KV): ~3.2 GB
- MTP draft compute buffer: ~1 GB
- Compute buffer: ~0.5 GB
- Total: ~21.9 GB / 23.42 GB usable on 24 GB GPU (HAMi overhead-accounted)

Comfortable headroom. Full 262K context is essentially free on this stack — the MoE-A3B + MTP path doesn't have the per-token cost scaling with context that dense models exhibit (Mamba-like state-space layers carry constant per-token cost regardless of position).

Practically: this app is now **fastest AND longest-context** Qwen3.6 27B/35B path on Olares One. Beats `llamacppqwen36beellamaone` v1.0.4 (107 t/s @ 262K, dense + DFlash) by **+130%** at the same context window. Beats `llamacppqwen36mtpone` v1.0.9 (74 t/s @ 262K, dense + MTP) by **+232%**. Same image as both (`aamsellem/llama-cpp-mtp:master-ad27757`), different model + architecture pays off entirely.

v1.0.1: complete rebuild. Switch to MTP path with `aamsellem/llama-cpp-mtp:master-ad27757` (ggml-org/llama.cpp master HEAD with PR #22673 MTP + #23269 cleanup + #23287 NVIDIA backend sampling + #22522 PDL Hopper+). Swap target from `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF` Q4_K_XL → `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF` Q3_K_XL (Q4_K_XL=22 GB OOMs with KV at 24 GB; Q3_K_XL=17.2 GB fits comfortably). Args: `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --ctx-size 32768 --cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0 --batch-size 512 --ubatch-size 512 --parallel 1 --flash-attn on --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'`.

- +37% vs Nemotron-Labs 30B-A3B NVFP4 + vLLM #40082 (182.14 t/s)
- +83% vs Gemma 4 26B-A4B vLLM (135.97 t/s)
- +132% vs BeeLlama Qwen3.6 27B + DFlash (107.54 t/s)
- +236% vs Qwen3.6 27B dense MTP same image (74.28 t/s)

Why so fast: MoE-A3B = only ~3B params active per token (per-token compute is roughly that of a 3B model) + MTP at 86.6% accept (drafts almost always validate) + NVIDIA backend sampling moves draft sampling onto CUDA backend (fewer host roundtrips). Effective: "3B-active speed with 35B-breadth quality." Context limited to 32K because KV cache + MTP draft buffer fits on 24 GB; higher contexts would need IQ4_XS or larger memory.

Title renamed "Qwen 36B-A3B One" → "Qwen36 35B-A3B MTP" for clarity. Port 8080 → 8000 (matches llama-server default in our master image).

v1.0.0: initial release. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Apache 2.0, April 2026). Same hybrid SSM/MoE architecture as 3.5 — reuses proven Olares One config (llama.cpp b8740, UD-Q4_K_XL, KV q4_0 with Hadamard rotation, batch 2048/ubatch 1024, 64K ctx). SWE-bench 70.0→73.4, Terminal-Bench 40.5→51.5.

This is the upstream resolution for the crash that v1.0.1 worked around via the HAMi-core memory limit bump. The original symptom on RTX 5090M sm_120 + Hermes Agent workload was a HAMi-core UINT64 underflow (`Device 0 OOM 18446744073709500456 / 25480396800`) which we now suspect was a downstream artifact of orphaned ring-buffer allocations after the underlying GPU ring crash — fixed upstream by `75ae2a6af`. Bench validated 2026-05-16 on Olares One: 105.52 t/s AVG @ 200K (10 runs, range 34.92) — perf parity with v1.0.1 (106.43 t/s, range 23.4) within noise. `system_fingerprint: b16-75ae2a6af` confirms commit. Long-context multi-turn validation (Hermes Agent at 100K+ accumulated context) is the real test — pending real-world user session.

Keeping `CUDA_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT_0=30000m` (bumped from 24300m in v1.0.1) as a safety belt until the user's next long agentic session confirms the fix holds. A future v1.0.3 will restore the strict 24300m once we have empirical proof the GPU ring fix eliminates the HAMi underflow downstream.

v1.0.1: workaround HAMi-core UINT64 accounting underflow that crashes the pod after long agentic sessions (~99K active context observed in Hermes Agent usage). The crash signature is `[HAMI-core ERROR]: Device 0 OOM 18446744073709500456 / 25480396800` — that 19-digit number is NOT a real allocation request, it's `2^64 - X` from an unsigned subtraction past zero in HAMi-core's internal allocator counter after many DFlash spec decoding micro-allocations. cublasSgemm_v2 fails → ggml_abort → pod restart.
Workaround: bump `CUDA_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT_0` 24300m → 30000m (above physical 24463 MB). HAMi-core stops gating allocations strictly, and BeeLlama hits the real physical VRAM limit cleanly via standard cudaMalloc errors if that ever happens. Tradeoff: HAMi GPU sharing no longer enforces this app's memory budget, so concurrent GPU apps could compete more aggressively. Acceptable since this app needs ~24 GB and any concurrent app would conflict anyway.
No bench change vs v1.0.0 (the inference path is identical) — this is purely a stability fix for sustained long-context sessions.

v1.0.0: initial release. Qwen3.6 27B vision-capable served via BeeLlama.cpp v0.1.2 with mmproj F16 vision projector + DFlash spec decoding + turbo3 KV cache. **First public bench of mmproj + DFlash + BeeLlama on consumer Blackwell sm_120**:

Validated 2026-05-15 on Olares One (10-run AVG, Space Invaders HTML prompt 2000 tokens each):
- **106.43 t/s AVG @ 200K context** (range 93.29-116.67, range 23.38)
- **101.98 t/s AVG @ 128K context** (10 runs, range 92.69-109.62)
- Vision smoke test: gradient PNG → correctly identified "Red" gradient

Trade-off vs llamacppqwen36beellamaone v1.0.2 (text-only, 107.54 t/s @ 262K):
- -1% throughput (106.43 vs 107.54)
- -23% max context (200K vs 262K)
- **+vision capability** (image input via OpenAI image_url content type)
- DFlash drafter still firing alongside mmproj (~27% accept rate validated on vision prompts)

43e83ecd.upgradeDescription:
v1.0.38: llama.cpp defaults — drop --mlock; ensure GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT=1 + --op-offload.
    v1.0.36: bump spec.accelerator to cover server + client container resource sums (v3 lint).
v1.0.35: migrate to apiVersion v3 shared chart (Olares 1.12.6+). Flatten server+client; workloadReplicas; no OLARES_USER_* in templates.
v1.0.18: **rollback BeeLlama → buun (preemptive Hermes regression fix)**. v1.0.17 swapped to `ghcr.io/anbeeld/beellama.cpp:server-cuda13-v0.3.1` for the maintained fork. A Discord user reported the same swap broke Hermes tool-calling on the sibling `llamacppqwen36a3bone` v2.0.6 (rolled back as v2.0.7). Reverting this chart's image to the known-good `aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:87c351d2` proactively to avoid the same regression — same asym q8_0/turbo4 KV + MTP + `--reasoning off` config as v1.0.17, just the buun image instead of BeeLlama. No bench delta expected (buun is the original source BeeLlama forked from).

v1.0.10: bump image `aamsellem/llama-cpp-mtp:master-ad27757` → `master-bb28c1f`. Picks up am17an's PR [#23461](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/23461) "server: free draft/MTP resources on sleep to fix VRAM leak" (validated by community Reddit thread on b9274) + #23433 "mtp: use inp_out_ids for skipping logit computation" + #23131 SWA null-buffer fix + #23287 NVIDIA backend sampling (same as v1.0.9). Bench re-validated 2026-05-22: 250.08 t/s AVG on Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (10 runs, +0.3% vs ad27757 — within noise). Real win is the VRAM leak fix for sustained agentic load. Same model bits, same flags, same context.

v1.0.9: SWAP to official ggml-org/llama.cpp master HEAD ad27757 (post b9219), drop custom am17an branch image. PR #22673 (MTP support) merged upstream 2026-05-16, then iterated on through three follow-up PRs we now pick up: #23269 (ggerganov 2026-05-19 "MTP clean-up") changed the default `--spec-draft-n-max` from 16 → 3, made `--spec-draft-p-min` functional again, fixed graph reuse for MTP drafting graphs (`batch.token && batch.embd` path), fixed ngram-k4v params propagation, and made all spec implementations see the accepted tokens (improving acceptance when chaining). #23287 (gaugarg-nv 2026-05-20 "Move to backend sampling for MTP draft path") is the NVIDIA-authored optimization that moves the draft-path sampling onto the CUDA backend — this is the headline. #22522 (Programmatic Dependent Launch for Hopper+ GPUs, sm_90+/sm_120 included) ships in this build too. Custom image `aamsellem/llama-cpp-mtp:master-ad27757` for amd64+CUDA13+sm_120 (Blackwell consumer mobile), built against ggml-org/llama.cpp upstream-pure (no fork patches). Includes the `-lcuda` linker workaround pending upstream issue [#23357](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/23357) which we filed against the same `CUDA::cuda_driver` PRIVATE-scope propagation bug Anbeeld already fixed on his BeeLlama fork (Anbeeld [#18](https://github.com/Anbeeld/beellama.cpp/issues/18)).

Bench validated 2026-05-21 on Olares One (10 runs, Space Invaders HTML 2000 tokens each, 262K ctx, q4_0 KV, n_max=3):
  - **74.28 t/s AVG** (range 72.60–75.14, σ=2.54 — ultra-tight)
  - **86.7% draft acceptance AVG** (83.4–88.6%)
  - vs v1.0.8 prod baseline (72.75 t/s / ~64% accept): **+2.1% throughput, +22 points acceptance**

The acceptance jump is the headline. The combination of n_max=3 (fewer drafts per step but each one validated more carefully) plus NVIDIA's backend-sampling rewrite makes MTP land in a much higher acceptance regime than the n_max=5 setup v1.0.8 used. Throughput is up modestly because the per-token overhead of MTP went down even though we're drafting fewer tokens per step.

Also bumps source HF repo: `unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-GGUF-MTP` → `unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF` (the former redirected, the latter is the canonical name post 2026-05-16 Unsloth release). Same `Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf` filename — model bits unchanged from v1.0.8.

Flag changes:
  - `--spec-type mtp` → `--spec-type draft-mtp` (flag renamed upstream 2026-05-13)
  - `--spec-draft-n-max 5` → `3` (matches new upstream default, validated as the better operating point on Blackwell mobile)
  - `--n-gpu-layers 99` → `-ngl 99` (cleaner)
  - default `CTX_SIZE` 128000 → 262144 (production ships at 262K)
  - `CUDA_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT_0` bumped 24300m → 30000m (HAMI workaround, no impact on inference)

v1.0.8: switch havenoammo Q2_K_XL → unsloth UD-Q3_K_XL. Validated 2026-05-12 on Olares One: 72.75 t/s AVG (10 runs, range 69.30-75.95), ZERO CUDA OOM at FULL 262K context with MTP n=5. Same speed as v1.0.7 (havenoammo Q2 was 72.14 t/s) BUT with Q3 quality tier (+5-8% vs Q2 on benchmarks). Surprising finding: havenoammo's Q3_K_XL (14.92 GB) hit runtime OOM at 262K (v1.0.5 bug), but unsloth's UD-Q3_K_XL (14.8 GB, ~120 MB smaller) is rock-stable at the same context + spec config. Different MTP integration metadata / memory layout. Strict upgrade vs v1.0.7: same context, same speed, better quality. Image still aamsellem/llamacpp-mtp:0.1.0 — will swap to ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda13-bNNNN once am17an's MTP PR #22673 merges upstream.
v1.0.7: get 262K back with MTP active. v1.0.6 was the safe-stable 128K fallback after v1.0.5's MTP CUDA OOM at 262K — but real users want both context AND MTP speed. Solution: swap havenoammo target Q3_K_XL (14.9 GB) → Q2_K_XL (12.3 GB), freeing 2.6 GB on top of the 1.9 GB Q3_K_XL already won over Q4_K_M. Total ~4.5 GB headroom recovered for MTP draft compute buffer — comfortably exceeds the ~2.5 GB gap that triggered `ggml_cuda_graph_evaluate_and_capture` exit-139 OOMs during `common_speculative_state_mtp::draft`. Restore CTX_SIZE → 262144, SPEC_DRAFT_N_MAX → 5. Trade-off: Q2_K_XL is a more aggressive Unsloth Dynamic quant (~5-8% quality drop on benchmarks vs Q3_K_XL). Direct bench validated 72.14 t/s STABLE. SUPERSEDED by v1.0.8 (unsloth UD-Q3_K_XL — same stability + Q3 quality).
v1.0.6: stability fix. v1.0.5's 262K context was boot-stable on our short-prompt validation bench (77 t/s @ 262K confirmed 2026-05-09) but at-runtime users hit CUDA OOM during MTP drafting: `ggml_cuda_graph_evaluate_and_capture` exit 139 inside `common_speculative_state_mtp::draft`. Cause is the same problem documented in v1.0.2: the MTP draft compute buffer grows with the cudagraph capture shapes the prompt actually exercises — boot's static allocator estimate isn't enough headroom even with Q3_K_XL's ~1.9 GB savings vs Q4_K_M. Reduce CTX_SIZE 262144 → 131072 (proven stable in v1.0.3, also a "long context" tier vs the fast 88 t/s vllmqwen36turbo27bone option) and SPEC_DRAFT_N_MAX 5 → 4 (one less draft frees a few hundred MB of compute buffer). Target stays havenoammo UD-Q3_K_XL — no rebuild. Users who really want 262K and accept occasional MTP crashes can override CTX_SIZE in their values. Expected: same 65-77 t/s range from v1.0.3/1.0.5, but rock-stable. SUPERSEDED by v1.0.7 (Q2_K_XL frees enough headroom to bring back 262K + MTP).
v1.0.5: target swap froggeric Q4_K_M-mtp (16.81 GB) → havenoammo UD-Q3_K_XL (14.92 GB, Unsloth Dynamic). Validated 2026-05-09 on Olares One: 77 t/s steady @ FULL 262K context with 75-80% draft acceptance (vs prior 65 t/s @ 128K, 64% accept). +18% speed +105% context +12 pts acceptance — single GGUF swap unlocks the Reddit-reported 80 t/s @ 262K recipe without any image rebuild. Q3_K_XL Unsloth Dynamic preserves critical layers in 6/8-bit while quantizing rest to 3-bit, giving better drafter alignment than standard Q4_K_M. The 1.9 GB target savings free up KV headroom for full 262K native context. Image still aamsellem/llamacpp-mtp:0.1.0 (am17an/mtp-clean), config flags unchanged. WARNING: runtime MTP CUDA OOM reported — fixed in v1.0.6 by reducing context to 128K.
v1.0.4: rename + description rework — this app is now positioned as the "long context" Qwen3.6 27B option (vs `vllmqwen36turbo27bone` "fast 88 t/s"). Title: "Qwen36 27B Long Context". Add HAMi-core `0m` parsing bug workaround (`CUDA_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT_0=24300m`) as precaution (the llama.cpp MTP path didn't trigger the bug in our tests but the override is harmless). 4 redundant Qwen3.6 27B apps removed from the market in same release: dflashqwen36one, lucedflashqwen36one, vllmqwen36dense27bone, llamacppqwen36dense27bone.
v1.0.3: bump CTX_SIZE 32000 → 128000 (sweet spot between v1.0.1's failed 262K and v1.0.2's safe 32K). Estimation: KV q4_0 on 16 full-attention layers ≈ 16KB/token → 128K ctx = ~2 GB KV (vs ~4.3 GB at 262K). Leaves ~4 GB free for MTP draft compute buffers (proven 32K worked with ~5.6 GB free at 78 t/s). 4× more context than v1.0.2 for agentic/long-context workflows. If OOM, fall back to v1.0.2 (32K) or move to IQ4_XS quant for more VRAM headroom at full context.
v1.0.2: revert CTX_SIZE 262144 → 32000. v1.0.1's 262K context made the MTP context allocation OOM at compute buffer stage (`graph_reserve: failed to allocate compute buffers / failed to create MTP context`). After model + KV q4_0 only ~1.8 GiB free, not enough for MTP draft head compute buffers. Pod fell back to non-MTP mode → 37 t/s baseline (vs expected 78 t/s). 32K context proven to fit on 24 GB with MTP active. froggeric's table claim "24 GB Q4_K_M q4_0 262K = 22.8 GB" doesn't account for MTP draft compute buffer overhead. Other v1.0.1 changes kept (q4_0 KV cache, spec-draft-n-max 5, batch/ubatch 512, model still froggeric/Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M-mtp.gguf with 7-fix chat template baked in). Future direction: try IQ3_M or IQ4_XS to free more VRAM for higher context.
v1.0.1: switch to froggeric/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF (community-recommended quants per ex-arman68's r/LocalLLaMA post 2026-05-06, 678 upvotes). Uses Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M-mtp.gguf (16.81 GB) with froggeric's 7-fix chat template baked in. Bumps CTX_SIZE 32000 → 262144 (full native 262K context, 8.2× larger), adds q4_0 KV cache (4-bit, quarter the KV memory at minor quality cost), bumps spec-draft-n-max 4 → 5 (community-recommended sweet spot for Qwen3.6 MTP), bumps batch/ubatch 256/64 → 512/512 (better prompt processing). Total VRAM ~22.8 GB at 262K — fits comfortably in 24 GB. Vision NOT enabled (currently crashes llama.cpp when used alongside MTP per upstream report 2026-05-06). Image still aamsellem/llamacpp-mtp:0.1.0 from am17an/mtp-clean PR #22673 branch.
v1.0.0: initial release. Qwen3.6 27B served via llama.cpp PR #22673 (am17an/mtp-clean, OPEN BLOCKED but tested 2026-05-04). Custom image aamsellem/llamacpp-mtp:0.1.0 built from am17an/mtp-clean branch (5 commits including MTP support + qwen35moe_mtp model wiring + GDN partial seq_rm). Target model RDson/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-Q4_K_M-GGUF (16.49 GB Q4_K_M with MTP head — standard unsloth quants strip the head, RDson preserved it). Validated 2026-05-04 on Olares One: 78.1 t/s avg over 3 Space Invaders prompts (Run1=74.91, Run2=80.60, Run3=78.78), +123% vs llama.cpp standard baseline (35 t/s). Stack is upstream-pure (one open PR + one HF GGUF) — once PR #22673 merges into ggml-org/llama.cpp master, this app will switch to ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda13-bNNNN with same flags.

v1.0.6: remove hardcoded --reasoning off — LLM_REASONING on|off|auto (default on). Bundled Qwen3.8 chat_template.jinja default via LLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE=bundled|froggeric|url; LLM_ENABLE_THINKING / LLM_PRESERVE_THINKING for --chat-template-kwargs.
v1.0.5: persistent crash/restart logging — wrap llama-server stdout/stderr into /olares/share/ai/model/llms/logs/.../server.<ts>.log and write last-exit.txt on non-0 rc.
v1.0.4: flip default `QWEN38_VARIANT` to `ridge_3_7bpw`. Goal: keep Q3-class footprint with slightly more architecture-aware quant mix for Qwen3.8 hybrid attention, while avoiding Q4_K_M long-context pressure on 24GB.
v1.0.3: add `QWEN38_VARIANT` selector for `ud_q3_k_xl` (default), `ud_q4_k_m`, or `ridge_3_7bpw`. Q4 gets safer defaults on 24GB (`ctx=131072`, `draft_n=3`) to reduce long-context first-token stalls / MTP buffer pressure. Research note updated: z-lab Qwen3.8 DFlash2 exists now, but as safetensors for vLLM/SGLang, not llama.cpp GGUF.
v1.0.2: reuse GGUFs already in Common/comfyui/model/llms (and subdirs) via symlink — official ComfyUI migrates External/ai/model/llms there; skip redownload.

Research (2026-08-15):
- Unsloth: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF (UD-Q3_K_XL / UD-Q4_K_M + mmproj-BF16). config has unsloth_fixed_mtp + mtp_num_hidden_layers=1 — --spec-type draft-mtp works without --model-draft.
- Ridge: empero-ai/Qwen3.8-27B-Ridge-GGUF keeps native MTP head, trims weight footprint to ~12.6 GB while staying in Q3-class size.

Stack for Olares One (RTX 5090M 24GB):

- Target default: Unsloth Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf (~13.1 GB) Dynamic 3.0 + embedded MTP

Pick vs siblings:

metadata.title: Qwen38 27B MTP Vision One
metadata.description: Qwen3.8 27B MTP + Vision — Unsloth UD-Q3 default, optional abliterated 12GB / Q4 / Ridge

spec.fullDescription:
Qwen3.8-27B dense VLM with embedded MTP speculative decoding.

Variants via QWEN38_VARIANT:
  - ud_q3_k_xl (default) — Unsloth Dynamic 3.0
  - abliterated — soyaakinohara 3.69bpw ~12GB MTP (uncensored)
  - ud_q4_k_m / ud_q4_k_xl — heavier Unsloth
  - ridge_3_7bpw — Empero Ridge optional

Thinking defaults to reasoning_effort=medium (override LLM_REASONING_EFFORT).
Sampling (Unsloth): thinking temp=1.0/top_p=0.95; instruct temp=0.7/top_p=0.8 when LLM_REASONING=off.
MTP: default embedded (GGUF baked). LLM_MTP_SOURCE=draft loads Unsloth MTP file as DFlash but caps ctx to 65K (196K draft KV OOMs on 24GB).
Abliterated: ctx 196608, KV q8_0/turbo4, draft n=3 (no multi-GPU tensor-split on One).
Stack: buun-llama-cpp + selectable GGUF + mmproj-BF16 + mmproj-gpu-swap.
OpenAI API via nginx client proxy and sharedEntrances.

Note: Unsloth agentic output caps (reasoning 262K / final 131K) exceed practical 24GB KV — use LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS / client max_tokens as needed. Native ctx up to 262144 via LLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW.

b7dce7d7.upgradeDescription:
v1.0.6: llama.cpp defaults — drop --mlock; ensure GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT=1 + --op-offload.
    v1.0.4: bump spec.accelerator to cover server + client container resource sums (v3 lint).
v1.0.3: migrate to apiVersion v3 shared chart (Olares 1.12.6+). Flatten server+client; workloadReplicas; no OLARES_USER_* in templates.
v1.0.18: **rollback BeeLlama → buun (preemptive Hermes regression fix)**. v1.0.17 swapped to `ghcr.io/anbeeld/beellama.cpp:server-cuda13-v0.3.1` for the maintained fork. A Discord user reported the same swap broke Hermes tool-calling on the sibling `llamacppqwen36a3bone` v2.0.6 (rolled back as v2.0.7). Reverting this chart's image to the known-good `aamsellem/buun-llama-cpp:87c351d2` proactively to avoid the same regression — same asym q8_0/turbo4 KV + MTP + `--reasoning off` config as v1.0.17, just the buun image instead of BeeLlama. No bench delta expected (buun is the original source BeeLlama forked from).

v1.0.10: bump image `aamsellem/llama-cpp-mtp:master-ad27757` → `master-bb28c1f`. Picks up am17an's PR [#23461](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/23461) "server: free draft/MTP resources on sleep to fix VRAM leak" (validated by community Reddit thread on b9274) + #23433 "mtp: use inp_out_ids for skipping logit computation" + #23131 SWA null-buffer fix + #23287 NVIDIA backend sampling (same as v1.0.9). Bench re-validated 2026-05-22: 250.08 t/s AVG on Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (10 runs, +0.3% vs ad27757 — within noise). Real win is the VRAM leak fix for sustained agentic load. Same model bits, same flags, same context.

v1.0.9: SWAP to official ggml-org/llama.cpp master HEAD ad27757 (post b9219), drop custom am17an branch image. PR #22673 (MTP support) merged upstream 2026-05-16, then iterated on through three follow-up PRs we now pick up: #23269 (ggerganov 2026-05-19 "MTP clean-up") changed the default `--spec-draft-n-max` from 16 → 3, made `--spec-draft-p-min` functional again, fixed graph reuse for MTP drafting graphs (`batch.token && batch.embd` path), fixed ngram-k4v params propagation, and made all spec implementations see the accepted tokens (improving acceptance when chaining). #23287 (gaugarg-nv 2026-05-20 "Move to backend sampling for MTP draft path") is the NVIDIA-authored optimization that moves the draft-path sampling onto the CUDA backend — this is the headline. #22522 (Programmatic Dependent Launch for Hopper+ GPUs, sm_90+/sm_120 included) ships in this build too. Custom image `aamsellem/llama-cpp-mtp:master-ad27757` for amd64+CUDA13+sm_120 (Blackwell consumer mobile), built against ggml-org/llama.cpp upstream-pure (no fork patches). Includes the `-lcuda` linker workaround pending upstream issue [#23357](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/23357) which we filed against the same `CUDA::cuda_driver` PRIVATE-scope propagation bug Anbeeld already fixed on his BeeLlama fork (Anbeeld [#18](https://github.com/Anbeeld/beellama.cpp/issues/18)).

Bench validated 2026-05-21 on Olares One (10 runs, Space Invaders HTML 2000 tokens each, 262K ctx, q4_0 KV, n_max=3):
  - **74.28 t/s AVG** (range 72.60–75.14, σ=2.54 — ultra-tight)
  - **86.7% draft acceptance AVG** (83.4–88.6%)
  - vs v1.0.8 prod baseline (72.75 t/s / ~64% accept): **+2.1% throughput, +22 points acceptance**

The acceptance jump is the headline. The combination of n_max=3 (fewer drafts per step but each one validated more carefully) plus NVIDIA's backend-sampling rewrite makes MTP land in a much higher acceptance regime than the n_max=5 setup v1.0.8 used. Throughput is up modestly because the per-token overhead of MTP went down even though we're drafting fewer tokens per step.

Also bumps source HF repo: `unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-GGUF-MTP` → `Jackrong/Qwopus3.6-27B-Coder-GGUF` (the former redirected, the latter is the canonical name post 2026-05-16 Unsloth release). Same `Qwopus3.6-27B-Coder-Q5_K_M.gguf` filename — model bits unchanged from v1.0.8.

Flag changes:
  - `--spec-type mtp` → `--spec-type draft-mtp` (flag renamed upstream 2026-05-13)
  - `--spec-draft-n-max 5` → `3` (matches new upstream default, validated as the better operating point on Blackwell mobile)
  - `--n-gpu-layers 99` → `-ngl 99` (cleaner)
  - default `CTX_SIZE` 128000 → 262144 (production ships at 262K)
  - `CUDA_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT_0` bumped 24300m → 30000m (HAMI workaround, no impact on inference)

v1.0.8: switch havenoammo Q2_K_XL → unsloth UD-Q3_K_XL. Validated 2026-05-12 on Olares One: 72.75 t/s AVG (10 runs, range 69.30-75.95), ZERO CUDA OOM at FULL 262K context with MTP n=5. Same speed as v1.0.7 (havenoammo Q2 was 72.14 t/s) BUT with Q3 quality tier (+5-8% vs Q2 on benchmarks). Surprising finding: havenoammo's Q3_K_XL (14.92 GB) hit runtime OOM at 262K (v1.0.5 bug), but unsloth's UD-Q3_K_XL (14.8 GB, ~120 MB smaller) is rock-stable at the same context + spec config. Different MTP integration metadata / memory layout. Strict upgrade vs v1.0.7: same context, same speed, better quality. Image still aamsellem/llamacpp-mtp:0.1.0 — will swap to ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda13-bNNNN once am17an's MTP PR #22673 merges upstream.
v1.0.7: get 262K back with MTP active. v1.0.6 was the safe-stable 128K fallback after v1.0.5's MTP CUDA OOM at 262K — but real users want both context AND MTP speed. Solution: swap havenoammo target Q3_K_XL (14.9 GB) → Q2_K_XL (12.3 GB), freeing 2.6 GB on top of the 1.9 GB Q3_K_XL already won over Q4_K_M. Total ~4.5 GB headroom recovered for MTP draft compute buffer — comfortably exceeds the ~2.5 GB gap that triggered `ggml_cuda_graph_evaluate_and_capture` exit-139 OOMs during `common_speculative_state_mtp::draft`. Restore CTX_SIZE → 262144, SPEC_DRAFT_N_MAX → 5. Trade-off: Q2_K_XL is a more aggressive Unsloth Dynamic quant (~5-8% quality drop on benchmarks vs Q3_K_XL). Direct bench validated 72.14 t/s STABLE. SUPERSEDED by v1.0.8 (unsloth UD-Q3_K_XL — same stability + Q3 quality).
v1.0.6: stability fix. v1.0.5's 262K context was boot-stable on our short-prompt validation bench (77 t/s @ 262K confirmed 2026-05-09) but at-runtime users hit CUDA OOM during MTP drafting: `ggml_cuda_graph_evaluate_and_capture` exit 139 inside `common_speculative_state_mtp::draft`. Cause is the same problem documented in v1.0.2: the MTP draft compute buffer grows with the cudagraph capture shapes the prompt actually exercises — boot's static allocator estimate isn't enough headroom even with Q3_K_XL's ~1.9 GB savings vs Q4_K_M. Reduce CTX_SIZE 262144 → 131072 (proven stable in v1.0.3, also a "long context" tier vs the fast 88 t/s vllmqwen36turbo27bone option) and SPEC_DRAFT_N_MAX 5 → 4 (one less draft frees a few hundred MB of compute buffer). Target stays havenoammo UD-Q3_K_XL — no rebuild. Users who really want 262K and accept occasional MTP crashes can override CTX_SIZE in their values. Expected: same 65-77 t/s range from v1.0.3/1.0.5, but rock-stable. SUPERSEDED by v1.0.7 (Q2_K_XL frees enough headroom to bring back 262K + MTP).
v1.0.5: target swap froggeric Q4_K_M-mtp (16.81 GB) → havenoammo UD-Q3_K_XL (14.92 GB, Unsloth Dynamic). Validated 2026-05-09 on Olares One: 77 t/s steady @ FULL 262K context with 75-80% draft acceptance (vs prior 65 t/s @ 128K, 64% accept). +18% speed +105% context +12 pts acceptance — single GGUF swap unlocks the Reddit-reported 80 t/s @ 262K recipe without any image rebuild. Q3_K_XL Unsloth Dynamic preserves critical layers in 6/8-bit while quantizing rest to 3-bit, giving better drafter alignment than standard Q4_K_M. The 1.9 GB target savings free up KV headroom for full 262K native context. Image still aamsellem/llamacpp-mtp:0.1.0 (am17an/mtp-clean), config flags unchanged. WARNING: runtime MTP CUDA OOM reported — fixed in v1.0.6 by reducing context to 128K.
v1.0.4: rename + description rework — this app is now positioned as the "long context" Qwen3.6 27B option (vs `vllmqwen36turbo27bone` "fast 88 t/s"). Title: "Qwen36 27B Long Context". Add HAMi-core `0m` parsing bug workaround (`CUDA_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT_0=24300m`) as precaution (the llama.cpp MTP path didn't trigger the bug in our tests but the override is harmless). 4 redundant Qwen3.6 27B apps removed from the market in same release: dflashqwen36one, lucedflashqwen36one, vllmqwen36dense27bone, llamacppqwen36dense27bone.
v1.0.3: bump CTX_SIZE 32000 → 128000 (sweet spot between v1.0.1's failed 262K and v1.0.2's safe 32K). Estimation: KV q4_0 on 16 full-attention layers ≈ 16KB/token → 128K ctx = ~2 GB KV (vs ~4.3 GB at 262K). Leaves ~4 GB free for MTP draft compute buffers (proven 32K worked with ~5.6 GB free at 78 t/s). 4× more context than v1.0.2 for agentic/long-context workflows. If OOM, fall back to v1.0.2 (32K) or move to IQ4_XS quant for more VRAM headroom at full context.
v1.0.2: revert CTX_SIZE 262144 → 32000. v1.0.1's 262K context made the MTP context allocation OOM at compute buffer stage (`graph_reserve: failed to allocate compute buffers / failed to create MTP context`). After model + KV q4_0 only ~1.8 GiB free, not enough for MTP draft head compute buffers. Pod fell back to non-MTP mode → 37 t/s baseline (vs expected 78 t/s). 32K context proven to fit on 24 GB with MTP active. froggeric's table claim "24 GB Q4_K_M q4_0 262K = 22.8 GB" doesn't account for MTP draft compute buffer overhead. Other v1.0.1 changes kept (q4_0 KV cache, spec-draft-n-max 5, batch/ubatch 512, model still froggeric/Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M-mtp.gguf with 7-fix chat template baked in). Future direction: try IQ3_M or IQ4_XS to free more VRAM for higher context.
v1.0.1: switch to froggeric/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF (community-recommended quants per ex-arman68's r/LocalLLaMA post 2026-05-06, 678 upvotes). Uses Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M-mtp.gguf (16.81 GB) with froggeric's 7-fix chat template baked in. Bumps CTX_SIZE 32000 → 262144 (full native 262K context, 8.2× larger), adds q4_0 KV cache (4-bit, quarter the KV memory at minor quality cost), bumps spec-draft-n-max 4 → 5 (community-recommended sweet spot for Qwen3.6 MTP), bumps batch/ubatch 256/64 → 512/512 (better prompt processing). Total VRAM ~22.8 GB at 262K — fits comfortably in 24 GB. Vision NOT enabled (currently crashes llama.cpp when used alongside MTP per upstream report 2026-05-06). Image still aamsellem/llamacpp-mtp:0.1.0 from am17an/mtp-clean PR #22673 branch.
v1.0.0: initial release. Qwen3.6 27B served via llama.cpp PR #22673 (am17an/mtp-clean, OPEN BLOCKED but tested 2026-05-04). Custom image aamsellem/llamacpp-mtp:0.1.0 built from am17an/mtp-clean branch (5 commits including MTP support + qwen35moe_mtp model wiring + GDN partial seq_rm). Target model RDson/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-Q4_K_M-GGUF (16.49 GB Q4_K_M with MTP head — standard unsloth quants strip the head, RDson preserved it). Validated 2026-05-04 on Olares One: 78.1 t/s avg over 3 Space Invaders prompts (Run1=74.91, Run2=80.60, Run3=78.78), +123% vs llama.cpp standard baseline (35 t/s). Stack is upstream-pure (one open PR + one HF GGUF) — once PR #22673 merges into ggml-org/llama.cpp master, this app will switch to ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda13-bNNNN with same flags.

Why it's so fast on Blackwell:
- Native NVFP4 tensor core path (no dequantize-and-multiply step). vLLM auto-selects `FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` GEMM + `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` MoE backend.
- MoE-A3B routing: 128 experts + 1 shared, only ~3B params active per token — comparable active-compute to a dense 3B model.
- Hybrid Mamba+Attention (`NemotronHForCausalLM`): half the layers are linear-cost state-space, half are quadratic attention.

The CUDA-graph trick: vLLM's default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graph capture reserves ~4 GB on top of the 18.78 GB model weights, OOM'ing on 24 GB GPUs. This chart ships with `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": 1, "max_cudagraph_capture_size": 4, "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4]}'` which switches to PIECEWISE-only with restricted capture sizes. CUDA graph pool drops from ~4 GB to **40 MB**, leaving enough headroom for the model + KV cache.

Constraints:
- `max_model_len = 4096` — at 32K context the KV cache wouldn't fit alongside model + graphs. Single-shot Q&A / code completion / agentic calls work fine; long PDFs / multi-turn coding need another app (e.g. `llamacppqwen36beellamaone` at 262K context).
- `max_num_seqs = 1` — single-stream, no concurrency. Multi-user case wants the Gemma 4 vision app instead.
- First request after pod boot: ~85s (CUDA graph capture + JIT compile). Subsequent requests hit 165 t/s immediately.
- NVFP4 quality vs INT4: ModelOpt warns "experimental". Kimi K2.5/K2.6 NVFP4 benches show within-1% MMLU divergence vs INT4 baseline. For this 30B I haven't done quality eval yet — recommended for fast prototyping, not (yet) for hard production tasks.

Stack:
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (vLLM v0.19.2rc1.dev107+g4eafc7292, pinned in chart)
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Labs-3-Elastic-30B-A3B-NVFP4` (HF, ~19 GB, NVIDIA Open Model License, public download — no HF token required)
- First launch downloads ~19 GB of safetensors. OpenAI-compatible chat API on port 8000.

Reference: [Blog post EN](https://aamsellem.com/blog/en/nemotron-nvfp4-blackwell-mobile-166-tps/) | [FR](https://aamsellem.com/blog/fr/nemotron-nvfp4-blackwell-mobile-166-tps/)

e74eca98.name: omnivoiceone
e74eca98.description: OmniVoice TTS (646 languages, voice cloning, voice design, 0.6B) — optimized for Olares One
e74eca98.title: OmniVoice TTS One
e74eca98.fullDescription:
OmniVoice TTS by k2-fsa — 646 languages, zero-shot voice cloning + voice design, 0.6B params.
RTX 5090M (24GB) + 96GB DDR5 + Core Ultra 9 275HX.
Only ~2-4 GB VRAM — runs alongside LLM and STT for a full voice pipeline.
40x faster than real-time. Apache 2.0 license.

===== HOW TO USE =====

In-cluster API (other apps in same Olares space): http://omnivoiceone:8000
App entrance (browser UI proxy): port 8080
Shared entrance (external agents): http://<route-id>.shared.olares.com

--- 1. Basic TTS (OpenAI-compatible) ---

curl -X POST http://omnivoiceone:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": "Hello world", "response_format": "wav"}' \
  -o out.wav

--- 2. Voice design (via `instruct` field) ---

Attributes are free-text, comma-separated. Categories:
  * gender:  male | female
  * age:     child | teen | adult | elderly
  * pitch:   very low | low | medium | high | very high
  * style:   whisper
  * accent:  american | british | (any)
  * dialect: sichuan | shaanxi | (zh only)

curl -X POST http://omnivoiceone:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "input": "This is a British female with a low pitch.",
    "instruct": "female, low pitch, british accent",
    "language_id": "en",
    "num_step": 32,
    "speed": 1.0
  }' -o out.wav

--- 3. Zero-shot voice cloning (multipart upload) ---

curl -X POST http://omnivoiceone:8000/v1/audio/clone \
  -F "text=Bonjour, ceci est ma voix clonée." \
  -F "ref_text=Voici une courte phrase de référence." \
  -F "ref_audio=@./my_voice_sample.wav" \
  -F "language_id=fr" \
  -F "num_step=32" \
  -o cloned.wav

--- 4. Voice cloning (JSON, base64 ref audio) ---

curl -X POST http://omnivoiceone:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "input": "Cloned output",
    "ref_text": "Reference transcription",
    "ref_audio_b64": "UklGRi...<base64 WAV>...AAA="
  }' -o out.wav

--- 5. Other endpoints ---

GET  /health              — liveness
GET  /web                 — web UI (app entrance redirects / here)
GET  /v1/models           — model list (OpenAI-compat)
GET  /v1/languages        — list all 646 supported language IDs

===== PARAMETERS =====

input / text       : text to synthesize (required)
instruct           : voice design attributes (string, optional)
ref_audio_b64      : base64-encoded WAV for voice cloning (optional)
ref_text           : transcription of the reference audio (required if ref_audio)
language_id        : ISO-like language code ("en", "fr", "zh", ...)
num_step           : diffusion steps (default 32; more = better quality, slower)
speed              : 0.5 .. 2.0 (default 1.0)
duration           : max audio length in seconds (default 10.0)
response_format    : "wav" (only format supported)

Downloads model on startup (~2GB) with visible logs.
Shared HF cache: /olares/share/ai/model/speech/huggingface (reused by all STT/TTS apps).
/health returns 200 immediately during model load; poll GET /health until ready:true before calling /v1/*. First boot model download may take 5-20 min.

Text-to-image benchmark chart for SenseNova-U1 on the upstream production stack: LightLLM (understanding / control) + LightX2V (image generation) with hybrid-mask FlashAttention-3 (`neopp_dense.json` → `attn_type: flash_attn3`).

Compare against sensenovau1serveone (single-process PyTorch + flash-attn 2.8.3 + optional GGUF). This chart does **not** replace that app — install one or both to A/B T2I latency.

Image: lightx2v/lightllm_lightx2v:20260407 (SenseNova-validated). Boot clones ModelTC/LightLLM @ neo_plus_clean and ModelTC/LightX2V, then launches `python -m lightllm.server.api_server` with `--enable_multimodal_x2i`.

Single-GPU profile (5090M 24GB): `--tp 1`, `--x2i_server_deploy_mode colocate`, `--x2i_server_used_gpus 1`, `--mem_fraction 0.68`, config `configs/neopp/neopp_dense.json`. Full BF16 safetensors from MODEL_REPO (~35GiB); GGUF not supported on this path.

API: OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/chat/completions` (modalities image/text). Health: `GET /health`. See OpenSenseNova examples/serving/client.py for request shapes.

Upstream reference (2×5090, TP2+CFG2 separate): ~0.415 s/step, ~23 s end-to-end for 2048×2048 T2I. Single-GPU colocate will be slower; goal is to see whether FA3 + LightX2V still beats the PyTorch reference server on Olares One.

In-pod benchmark (after model ready):
`python /app-src/benchmark_t2i.py --warmup`
Compare to sensenovau1serveone: `POST /api/v1/t2i` with aspect_ratio 1:1 (2048²) and enable INFERENCE_TIMING=1 on that chart.

Switch model: set values.yaml `model.repo` to
sensenova/SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V2 or
sensenova/SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Interleaved
(full safetensors; no GGUF on this LightLLM path — expect CPU/offload pressure on 24GB).

11e9726c.name: sensenovau1serveone
11e9726c.description: SenseNova-U1 T2I, VQA, editing, and interleave via REST API and Gradio
11e9726c.title: SenseNova U1 Serve One
11e9726c.fullDescription:
Runs OpenSenseNova SenseNova-U1 from https://github.com/OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-U1 with one GPU load and four modalities exposed as JSON APIs for orchestrators or humans via Gradio.
Container image: pytorch/pytorch:2.11.0-cuda13.0-cudnn9-devel (CUDA 13 + Python 3.12).
Boot: shallow-clone SenseNova-U1 under workspace volume, pip install -e with --no-deps so the image Torch/CUDA build is not replaced by PyPI torch==2.8 pins from upstream pyproject, then install pinned transformers stack + FastAPI/Gradio from bundled requirements.txt.
Config and tokenizer: init snapshot_download of sensenova/SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT into MODEL_DIR (MODEL_PATH). With USE_GGUF_WEIGHTS=1, snapshot skips *.safetensors shards (GGUF supplies weights); init then hf_hub_downloads config.json, tokenizer_config.json, vocab.json, merges.txt, added_tokens.json, special_tokens_map.json so tokenizer assets are always present; upstream load_model_and_tokenizer still needs that HF layout for architecture + tokenizer.
Default weights: merger GGUF from https://huggingface.co/smthem/SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Merger-gguf — init downloads GGUF_FILE plus optional GGUF_DOWNLOAD_FILES (comma list); default prefetch includes all four public GGUFs (~67GiB total — trim ConfigMap to one file if disk-constrained). Runtime: optional JSON field gguf_filename on each POST selects basename under GGUF_DIR and reloads weights when it changes; Gradio exposes same dropdown. Variant hints in GET /api/v1/capabilities under gguf_variant_guide (8step-Q4 fastest/low VRAM; Q6 balance; SFT-fm-* instruction-tuned merger; Q8 heaviest).
Disable GGUF: set USE_GGUF_WEIGHTS=0 in sensenovau1-serve-env (full safetensors from MODEL_DIR only).
Layer offload: VRAM_MODE defaults to full on Olares One (weights stay on GPU). Set low | balanced only to save VRAM at large speed cost (see upstream VRAM_MODE_OPTIONS).
Attention: SenseNova OSS uses FA2-class flash_attn.flash_attn_func (not FA3/FA4). Default INSTALL_FLASH_ATTN=1 installs a Blackwell sm_120 prebuilt wheel (cached under /workspace/wheels); soft-fails to SDPA if install/import fails — no in-pod source compile (that caused restart loops). For FA3 hybrid path use sensenovau1lightllmone (LightX2V) instead.
HTTP: GET / redirects to Gradio at /ui; GET /api/v1/capabilities; POST /api/v1/t2i | vqa | editing | interleave; OpenAPI at /docs.
HF model variants (same NeoChat MoT API surface): default sensenova/SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT; swap MODEL_REPO to SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V2 or SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Interleaved. Infographic/Interleaved need USE_GGUF_WEIGHTS=0 (merger GGUF is base-only) + VRAM_MODE=balanced on 24GB.

c0481b5c.name: sensenovavisionone
c0481b5c.title: SenseNova Vision One
c0481b5c.fullDescription:
SenseNova-Vision-7B-MoT — unified multimodal CV as generation
(depth, normals, segmentation, detection, OCR, multi-view geometry).

Hardware: Olares One — RTX 5090M 24GB + 96GB DDR5.

Runtime image: pytorch/pytorch:2.12.0-cuda13.0-cudnn9-devel (sm_120).

Weights: sensenova/SenseNova-Vision-7B-MoT (~30GB ema.safetensors)
Source: https://github.com/OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-Vision
License: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial)

VRAM note: upstream Gradio demo recommends ~80GB. Default load is
bitsandbytes NF4 from the same bf16 safetensors (no separate NF4/GGUF repo),
plus accelerate device_map + CPU offload (SENSENOVA_MAX_MEM_PER_GPU=20GiB).
Set SENSENOVA_DTYPE=bf16 for full precision if you have headroom.

Boot (LingBot / Krea pattern):
- soft-ready HTTP on :7860 before uv/pip/HF download
- uv pip --target /workspace/sensenovavisionone/site-packages + uv-cache
- purge torch shadow from site-packages (image owns torch)
- flash_attn hard-import patched → SDPA (Blackwell / no FA wheel)
- bootstrap log → /workspace/sensenovavisionone/bootstrap.log

UI: / and /ui · REST POST /api/v1/predict · timings GET /api/v1/timings · health GET /health

b3078d17.fullDescription:

b3078d17.upgradeDescription:
v1.0.23: bump spec.accelerator to cover server + client container resource sums (v3 lint).
v1.0.22: migrate to apiVersion v3 shared chart (Olares 1.12.6+). Flatten server+client; workloadReplicas; no OLARES_USER_* in templates.
v1.0.5: **128K native context restored** (was 64K in v1.0.4). Tested 192K + 256K — both work technically but 192K+ uses RoPE scaling beyond Gemma 4's native 128K training range, with attention drift / hallucination risk on tokens past 128K. 256K explicitly OOMs (vLLM reports estimated max 203584). 128K is Gemma 4's sweet spot: trained on it, validated quality. Bench 2026-05-23: **250.80 t/s AVG @ 128K** (10 runs, range 246.53-254.39, spread 7.86, σ ≈ 2.5) — identical to v1.0.4 @ 64K (250.54), confirming throughput is decode-bound not context-bound (Gemma 4 sliding-window attention scales gracefully).

v1.0.4: **MTP unlocked, +85% throughput, vision preserved**. Bump vLLM image `tokenspeed-preview` → **`v0.21.0-cu129`** (Gemma4 MTP officially merged in vLLM PR #41745). Adds `--speculative-config '{"model":"google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant","method":"gemma4_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`. The official Google `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant` drafter (840 MB safetensors) replaces the cycle-bug-prone z-lab DFlash drafter.

**Bench validated 2026-05-23 on Olares One**: **250.54 t/s AVG** (10 clean runs, range 247.84-252.97 = spread 5.13, σ ≈ 1.7, **NO cycle bug**), **86.4% MTP draft acceptance** (25920/29997 tokens accepted across 9999 drafts). Vision validated (64×64 PNG → "Red" correct).

- **+85% vs v1.0.0 no-spec** (135.97 → 250.54 t/s)
- **+12% vs v1.0.4 DFlash** (224 t/s AVG with degradation cycle bug, abandoned)
- **Matches `llamacppqwen36a3bone` MTP champion** (250 t/s) — equal speed, with vision as bonus
- Tight spread (5.13 vs DFlash ~150 range with cycle): zero "5-fast/4-slow" pattern

Context reduced 128K → 64K to leave VRAM headroom for MTP draft buffer + larger compute graph. 64K still covers Hermes-Agent tool histories generously. For longer-context Gemma 4 without MTP/vision, use `vllmgemma4dflashone` (text-only, DFlash, 224 t/s @ 128K).

Stack:
- vLLM v0.21.0 (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.21.0-cu129`) — official Gemma4 MTP support
- Target: `cyankiwi/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-AWQ-4bit` (compressed-tensors WNA16-Marlin, ~17 GB)
- Drafter: `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant` (Google official, 840 MB)
- `--attention-backend triton_attn` (required for vision, head_dim heterogeneity)
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}'`
- OpenAI-compatible tool calling preserved (`--tool-call-parser gemma4`)

Why it matters for agents: Hermes-Agent style tool calling now runs at champion speed (250 t/s) on a vision-capable model. Single endpoint handles text + image + tool calling + structured output, with stable latency.

v1.0.2: enable **OpenAI-compatible tool calling** for Hermes Agent and other agent frameworks. Adds `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4` to vLLM server args. Gemma 4 uses a custom non-JSON serialization format (`<|tool_call>call:func_name{key:<|"|>value<|"|>}<tool_call|>`) for tool calls — vLLM's `gemma4` parser handles the decode→OpenAI tool_calls translation. Without this flag, requests with `tool_choice: "auto"` return HTTP 400. No throughput impact (parser only kicks in when tools are present in the request). Validated on Hermes Agent: long-context summarization + tool calling now works end-to-end against `https://llm.<user>.olares.com/v1` with model `gemma-4-26b-vision`.

v1.0.1: bump max_model_len 16384 → **131072 (128K)** for Marc's office workhorse use case (2-3 concurrent users, long PDF processing, vision input). Also bumps gpu_memory_utilization 0.85 → 0.92 to fit the larger KV cache. **Zero throughput regression** — validated 2026-05-15 bench: **135.85 t/s AVG @ 128K** (10 runs, range 135.52-136.06, range 0.54). Identical to v1.0.0 16K bench (135.97 t/s, range 0.56). 8× context for free. Marc's spec hit: vision + 128K + >100 t/s + PagedAttention (multi-user).

v1.0.0: initial release. Gemma 4 26B-A4B vision-capable served via vLLM, optimized for Olares One. Validated 2026-05-14 night-bench: **135.97 t/s AVG** (10 clean runs, range 135.67-136.23, exceptional stability 0.56) on RTX 5090M sm_120 mobile Blackwell.

Why vLLM instead of llama.cpp for this app:
- +9.7% throughput vs llama.cpp atomic fork (123.97 t/s validated same hardware same prompt)
- Native multimodal architecture (Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration) — no separate mmproj download, vision encoder bundled in model
- Mainline path (vs atomic fork dependency)
- Future v1.0.1 can add z-lab DFlash drafter for target 200+ t/s with vision (currently DFlash drafter compat with multimodal under validation)

Stack:
- Image: vllm/vllm-openai:tokenspeed-preview-x86_64-ubuntu2404
- Target: cyankiwi/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-AWQ-4bit (compressed-tensors WNA16-Marlin, ~17 GB on GPU, native Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration with vision_config + audio_config)
- Vision: native (image_token_id 258880, no separate mmproj projector needed)
- KV cache: FP8 (vLLM native)
- Attention backend: triton_attn (Gemma 4 head_dim heterogeneous requires this — flash_attn errors with "partial multimodal token full attention not supported")
- Context: **131072 (128K)** — pushed from initial 16K, zero throughput regression validated
- Throughput tuning: max-num-seqs=4, max-num-batched-tokens=8192, gpu-memory-utilization=0.85, --enable-prefix-caching
- HAMi workaround: CUDA_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT_0=24400m (Olares default 0m parses as 0 bytes by HAMi-core)
- Vision smoke test 2026-05-14: 64x64 base64 PNG gradient → model correctly responded "Red" in 0.73s wall time

18a6f781.upgradeDescription:
v1.0.25: bump spec.accelerator to cover server + client container resource sums (v3 lint).
v1.0.24: migrate to apiVersion v3 shared chart (Olares 1.12.6+). Flatten server+client; workloadReplicas; no OLARES_USER_* in templates.
v1.0.7: **rollback v1.0.6 vLLM v0.23.0 bump** — engine init crash. Root cause: PR #43445 "Causal DFlash" landed in v0.23.0 and made `use_non_causal=True` unsupported on every attention backend (`TRITON_ATTN`, `FLASH_ATTN`, `FLASHINFER`, `FLEX_ATTENTION`, `TURBOQUANT` — all reject non-causal). Gemma 4's bidirectional prefix requires non-causal, so v0.23.0 boot fails with:

```
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda with AttentionSelectorConfig(
  head_size=128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, kv_cache_dtype=fp8, ..., use_non_causal=True)
```

"Causal DFlash" was meant to harden DFlash spec-decode (fixing the 220→60 t/s degradation cycle we observed), but it dropped the non-causal path entirely. Until vLLM ships a release that re-supports non-causal DFlash for Gemma 4, we stay on `tokenspeed-preview-x86_64-ubuntu2404` (vLLM 0.20.2rc1.dev67, 2026-05-06).

No config changes vs v1.0.4. Bench remains 224 t/s AVG (degradation cycle still latent).

v1.0.6: **bump image to vLLM v0.23.0** (pre-release tagged 2026-06-13 ~01:30 UTC). v0.23.0 brings 408 commits / 200 contributors, including the trio directly relevant to our 220→60 t/s degradation cycle:

- **PR #43445 Causal DFlash** — hardens DFlash spec-decode internal state machine
- **PR #42971 prefix-cache corruption fix** — likely fixes the "no spec decoding active" intermittent state we observed in [reference_dflash_gemma4_nspec_sweep](memory) where 5 fast runs at 220 t/s would be followed by 4 slow runs at 60 t/s
- **PR #43733 lookahead-slot allocation fix** — DFlash schedule correctness
- **PR #40923 Marlin MoE on SM 12.x** — first sm_120 MoE Marlin kernel in mainline (was previously only `tokenspeed-preview`)

Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0-x86_64-ubuntu2404` (9.2 GB, CUDA 13.0 — within Olares driver 590.44.01 cap of 13.1). Replaces `tokenspeed-preview-x86_64-ubuntu2404` (8.8 GB, vLLM 0.20.2rc1.dev67).

Same config otherwise: n_spec=8 (v1.0.4 optimum), AWQ target, fp8 KV, triton_attn, max-num-seqs=4, max-num-batched-tokens=8192, HAMi cap 24400m.

Bench TBD — multiple 10+ run sequences expected to validate the degradation cycle is GONE. Baseline to beat: 223.90 t/s AVG / 216.86 MIN / 235.22 MAX from v1.0.4.

v1.0.4: night-bench n_spec sweep on 5090M mobile 24GB found optimum at n_spec=8 (vs v1.0.0 at n=13). Validated 2026-05-11 over 5 clean Space Invaders runs (max_tokens=2000): AVG 223.90 t/s, MIN 216.86, MAX 235.22 — +5% over v1.0.0 baseline (214 avg), +11% over v1.0.3 (201 avg). Full sweep n∈{6,8,10,11,12,13,15,17,20} shows peak at n=8 then linear regression at n≥10. Tech-Practice article's n=15 recommendation is desktop-only (5090 32GB, 1.79 TB/s bandwidth) — mobile 5090M (24GB, 896 GB/s = 50% bandwidth) needs shallower drafts because compute buffer per spec token consumes proportionally more VRAM. Other diffs from v1.0.0: explicit --attention-backend triton_attn (was implicit auto-select). KV cache fp8, max-num-batched-tokens 8192, max-num-seqs 4 unchanged.
v1.0.3: fix v1.0.2 OOM. Bumping max-num-batched-tokens 8192→32768 with n_spec=15 blew the compute buffers — needed +352 MiB on a 23.42 GB GPU already at 23.18 GB. Revert batched-tokens to 8192 (v1.0.0 value). Only diff vs v1.0.0 now: num_speculative_tokens 13→15 + explicit --attention-backend triton_attn (previously implicit auto-select). Expected: marginal +2-5% over 214 t/s (deeper draft only, no scheduler bump). Bench result confirmed REGRESSION (-6% to 201 avg) — fixed by ship n_spec=8 in v1.0.4.
v1.0.2: fix v1.0.1 crash. Gemma 4 multimodal tokens forbid flash_attn even for the drafter ("partial multimodal token full attention not supported"). Drop attention_backend:flash_attn from SPEC_CONFIG, keep --attention-backend triton_attn explicit for target. Remaining diffs vs v1.0.0: (1) num_speculative_tokens 13 → 15, (2) max-num-batched-tokens 8192 → 32768. CRASHED with OOM in cudagraph capture (23.18/23.42 GB used, +352 MiB needed) — fixed in v1.0.3 by reverting batched-tokens.
v1.0.1: apply z-lab canonical DFlash config (per Tech-Practice RTX 5090 sweep, 2026-05-09). Three changes: (1) num_speculative_tokens 13 → 15 (deeper draft, accept tail), (2) explicit attention backend split — flash_attn inside speculative-config for drafter, --attention-backend triton_attn for target (Gemma 4 head_dim hetero requires triton for target), (3) max-num-batched-tokens 8192 → 32768. Same image (tokenspeed-preview), same model (cyankiwi AWQ), same fp8 KV. Expected: +5-10% vs 214 t/s baseline on 5090M mobile (50% bandwidth vs desktop 5090). CRASHED at boot due to flash_attn + multimodal incompat — fixed in v1.0.2. Rollback to v1.0.0 if regression.
v1.0.0: initial release. Gemma 4 26B-A4B (compressed-tensors WNA16-Marlin, ~17.5 GB VRAM) target + z-lab DFlash drafter (~0.8 GB) via vLLM tokenspeed-preview-x86_64 image (vLLM 0.20.2rc1.dev67, perf preview, 2026-05-06). Validated bench on Olares One 2026-05-09: **214 t/s steady state** (Space Invaders prompt, 2000 tokens, 3-run avg of runs 2-3, +53% over the llama.cpp + AtomicChat MTP baseline 140 t/s). First public DFlash Gemma 4 result on Blackwell consumer mobile. Drafter pos-0 acceptance ~28% (lower than DFlash typical 60%, target+drafter alignment limited on consumer 24 GB). Forced TRITON_ATTN backend (Gemma 4 head_dim 256/512 heterogeneous) is the main perf cap. Required: max-num-seqs=4 + max-num-batched-tokens=8192 to make num_speculative_tokens=13 schedulable, kv-cache-dtype=fp8, gpu-memory-utilization=0.92, CUDA_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT_0=24400m for HAMi.
